meta.title: SidePerks — get paid for watching ads and taking surveys
meta.description: Watch short video ads and answer quick surveys on your phone. Points are pegged to the cedi and you withdraw to Mobile Money or crypto. Free to join, no card needed.

hero.title: Get paid for your
hero.lead: SidePerks pays you points for watching short video ads and answering quick surveys on your phone. {points} points is GHS 1, and the free plan gives you {freeAds} ads every single day.
hero.note: Free to join. No card, no deposit, no minimum.
hero.shotAlt: The SidePerks ads feed on a phone, showing video ads with the points each one pays

ways.title: Two ways to earn, and one
ways.lead: Watching is live today. Inviting friends is live today. Affiliate offers are the next thing being built, and we would rather say so than dress it up.

watch.title: Watch video ads and take surveys
watch.body: The main way to earn on SidePerks. Short video ads with a question or two, and surveys where your honest opinion is the whole point. {freeAds} a day on the free plan, and more on every paid one.

points.videos: Short videos, most under two minutes
points.surveys: Surveys with no right or wrong answers
points.upfront: You see what an ad pays before you open it
points.instant: Points land in your balance the moment you finish

invite.title: Invite your friends
invite.body: Every account comes with a personal invite link. Share it, and you earn a bonus once the people who joined through it start watching.

affiliate.title: Affiliate offers
affiliate.body: Promoting partner products for a commission. This one is not built yet — it is on the roadmap, not in the app, and there is nothing here to sign up for.

how.title: From sign-up to points in
how.lead: No interview, no documents, no waiting to be approved. You can be earning within a minute of creating an account.

signup.title: Create your account
signup.body: An email address and a password. That is the whole form, and you are on the free plan straight away.

watch.title: Open an ad or a survey
watch.body: Your feed shows what is available to you today and exactly how many points each one pays.

answer.title: Answer the question
answer.body: Video ads ask a short question to check you were watching. Surveys simply ask what you think.

earn.title: Points hit your balance
earn.body: Credited the moment you finish, shown in points and in cedis, and listed in your statement.

earning.title: The real app, not a
earning.lead: Every screen below is a genuine screenshot of SidePerks running, in the theme you are reading this in.

feed.title: Every ad tells you what it pays, before you open it
feed.body: No mystery rewards and no bait. The points, the length and the number of questions are on the card, so you can decide whether it is worth your data before you spend any.

points.length: Video length shown before you commit
points.tabs: Videos and surveys kept in separate tabs
points.cap: A clear count of what is left today — {freeAds} free

feed.shotAlt: The SidePerks ads feed, with video ad cards each showing the points it pays

balance.title: Your balance in cedis, not just points
balance.body: Points are pegged to the cedi at {points} to GHS 1, so you always know what a balance is actually worth. The rate in force is written onto every entry, so nothing reprices behind you.

points.cedis: Balance shown in GHS first, points underneath
points.statement: A full statement of every point in and out
points.chart: Earnings and ads watched over the last 30 days
points.withdraw: Withdraw to your own Mobile Money or crypto account

balance.shotAlt: The SidePerks home screen showing a balance in Ghana cedis, the daily ad count and lifetime earnings

plans.title: Watch more, earn
plans.lead: The free plan never expires. A paid plan raises your daily limit, pays more points per ad, and lowers the balance you need before you can withdraw.

free.title: {name} plan — GHS 0
free.body: {ads} ads a day for your first {days} days, and you can withdraw from {threshold} points. No card needed to start.

plans.stacking: Plans stack. Hold more than one and the daily limits add up, the earning bonuses add together, and the lowest withdrawal threshold is the one that applies. Every plan runs for a fixed period and nothing renews on its own — you are never charged again without asking.

invite.title: Your link, your
invite.lead: Every account comes with a personal invite link. Send it on WhatsApp, and when the people who joined through it start watching, you earn a bonus on top of your own earnings.

share.title: Share your link
share.body: One tap copies a ready-made message with your link in it, or opens your phone's share sheet straight into WhatsApp.

join.title: They join
join.body: Your code is filled in for them automatically, so nobody has to remember or type anything.

watch.title: They start watching
watch.body: Your bonus is tied to real activity rather than to a signup — which is what keeps the programme worth anything.

bonus.title: You get your bonus
bonus.body: Credited to your balance like any other earning and listed in your statement. It is the same amount for everybody — what an invite is worth depends on what they do, not on which plan you hold.

safety.title: Built like something that holds your
safety.lead: Every item here is already in the app. None of it is on a roadmap.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor sign-in
twoFactor.body: Optional authenticator-app sign-in, with backup codes for when you lose the phone. No sign-in code is ever emailed to you.

pin.title: Withdrawal PIN
pin.body: A separate 4-digit PIN for moving money, stored only as a hash, and locked for 15 minutes after five wrong tries.

accounts.title: Your accounts only
accounts.body: Withdrawals go to Mobile Money or crypto accounts you set up yourself, and changing one starts a 48-hour cool-off.

peg.title: Pegged to the cedi
peg.body: The points-to-cedi rate in force is written onto every entry in your statement, so a balance cannot quietly reprice.

data.title: Only what the account needs
data.body: Passwords, PINs and backup codes are stored as hashes, never as text, and the servers are in the EU.

oneAccount.title: One account per person
oneAccount.body: Duplicate and automated accounts are removed. That is what keeps the reward pool for people who actually watch.

faq.title: Straight
faq.lead: Better to have this clear before you sign up than after.

free.a: Yes. The free plan gives you {freeAds} ads a day for your first {days} days. After that a paid plan is needed to keep earning — the points you already have stay yours. Nothing else is locked behind them: plans raise your daily limit and the points you get per ad.

worth.q: What is a point actually worth?
worth.a: {points} points is GHS 1. That rate is stored on every entry in your statement, so points you earned last month are still worth what they were worth when you earned them.

withdraw.a: Once your balance passes {threshold} points — the same threshold for everybody, whatever plan you hold. Payouts switch on when our payout licensing is complete; until then you can set up your payout account and keep earning, and the app tells you plainly where a request stands rather than pretending.

questions.q: Do I have to answer questions?
questions.a: Some video ads carry a short question to check you were watching, and some are watch-only. Surveys are a different thing: they are asking for your opinion, so there is no right answer and nothing to get wrong.

methods.a: To a Mobile Money account — MTN, Telecel or AirtelTigo — or to a crypto wallet in USDT. You choose which and set it up yourself in your profile, and withdrawals can only ever go to an account saved on your own profile.

devices.q: Will it work on my phone?
devices.a: It is built for inexpensive Android phones and slow connections, and it is tested down to iOS 12 and Android 6. There is nothing to install — it runs in your browser.

cta.title: Your spare minutes are already
cta.lead: Create a free account and watch your first ad today — {freeAds} of them a day, every day, at no cost.
cta.note: Under a minute to join. An email address and a password, nothing else.

footer.blurb: SidePerks pays you for watching short video ads and taking surveys on your phone. Built in Ghana, for Ghana.

panel.body: Short videos, one quick question, real points. Turn your spare minutes into mobile money or crypto.

editor.saveRejected: Some fields still need attention. They are marked below.
editor.basicsHint: What the ad is called in the feed and who it is for.
editor.title: Title
editor.advertiserHint: A label for reporting. There is no advertiser account behind it.
editor.descriptionHint: One line under the title on the card. Optional.
editor.descriptionPlaceholder: What the viewer is about to watch
editor.videoHint: A YouTube link, or a file uploaded to our own storage.
editor.durationHint: Read from an uploaded file automatically. Needed for a watch-only ad.
editor.minWatchHint: Before a question may be answered. Empty means the whole video.
editor.youtubeHint: Paste the watch, share, embed or Shorts URL — the ID is taken from it.
editor.videoFileHint: MP4, WebM or MOV, up to 100 MB. Uploads as soon as it is chosen.
editor.thumbnailHint: The image on the card. Without one the card draws its own cover.
editor.thumbnailHintYoutube: Optional — without one, YouTube's own still is used.
editor.questionsHintVideo: A video may interrupt with a question at any second, or ask at the end, or ask nothing at all and pay on watch time.
editor.questionsHintSurvey: A survey is not a quiz. Tick a right answer only where there genuinely is one — otherwise any answer is accepted and recorded.
editor.questionsLocked: {count, plural, one {# person has} other {# people have}} already completed this ad, so its questions are fixed. Rewriting them would rewrite what the advertiser’s research says. Everything else here is still editable; to change the questions, duplicate this ad and publish the copy.
editor.noQuestionsVideo: No questions. This ad will pay on watch time alone.
editor.noQuestionsSurvey: A survey needs at least one question.
editor.questionPlaceholder: What did the advert say the offer was?
editor.cueHint: Playback pauses at this second and the question appears.
editor.cueEndHint: The question waits until the video finishes.
editor.optionsHint: Select the right answer only if there is one. With none selected this is an opinion question: any choice is accepted and recorded.
editor.markCorrect: Mark option {n} as the right answer
editor.gradeAnswerHint: Off means any typed answer is accepted and recorded.
editor.acceptedAnswerHint: Compared without case or spacing mattering.
editor.conditionsHint: Show this question based on an earlier answer.
editor.cascadeNote: Skipping cascades: if the question above is never shown, this one is not shown either — and nor is anything depending on it.
editor.audienceHint: Which plans this ad is aimed at.
editor.audienceEveryone: Everyone sees this ad, whatever plan they hold.
editor.audienceInclusive: Holders of a higher plan also see it, so upgrading never shrinks somebody’s pool. Turn that off under Platform settings for exact targeting.
editor.statusHint: Only a live ad is served, and only inside its schedule.
editor.exhaustedNote: This ad has delivered its whole budget and stopped serving. Raise the number of completions to run it again.
editor.archivedNote: Archived ads are never served. Move it back to draft to work on it again.
editor.timesUtc: Times are UTC, which is Ghana time all year. Leave empty for no limit.
editor.rewardHint: What a free-plan user earns. Paid plans multiply it.
editor.unlimitedHint: Runs until you pause it. Use deliberately — nothing stops the spend.
editor.budgetHint: Completions paid for. The ad stops serving when they run out.
editor.weightHint: Higher serves more often within the eligible pool. 100 is normal.
editor.costNote: Budget × reward at the current rate, before any plan multiplier.
editor.summaryQuestions: {count, plural, =0 {No questions — pays on watch time} one {# question} other {# questions}}

editor.archiveHint: People have watched it, so it is archived rather than deleted — the attempts behind their earnings have to survive.
editor.confirmDeleteBody: It goes with its questions and cannot be recovered.
editor.confirmArchiveBody: It stays on the record but is never served again.

subscriptions.hiddenInstead: {name} has been bought, so it was taken off sale rather than deleted — the payments behind it are part of the statement.

band.title: Sells from {from} to GHS {to}
band.body: A buyer choosing inside that range earns between {from}× and {to}× — the rate slides towards {next} as they pay more. All of them get {ads} ads a day; only the value of an ad changes.
band.topBody: This is the top of the ladder, so there is nothing above it to slide towards. Buyers pay exactly {price}.
band.line: Buyers choose any amount from {from} to GHS {to}.
band.topLine: The top plan sells at exactly {price} — there is no plan above it to set a ceiling.
band.perCedi: At this floor, GHS 1 buys +{pct}% on the earning rate. Plans higher up the ladder deliberately buy less per cedi.
band.neighbour: This also moves {name}: its range was {from} – {was} and becomes {from} – {to}. Everyone who buys {name} after this earns at the new rate.
band.topRangeBody: Paying the floor earns {from}×, paying {price} earns {to}×, and anything between lands on the line. Ads a day stay at {ads} whatever they pay.

unbuyable.body: Its price is at or above {next}, which sits directly above it — so the range has nothing in it and the server refuses every amount. Price it below {next}, or move it above {next} in the sort order.

earningInversion.body: {next} sits above this plan but earns at a LOWER rate, so inside this band the rate falls as the price rises: a buyer moving the slider up would watch their earning go down. Raise {next} or lower this one.

adsInversion.short: The plan above shows fewer ads
adsInversion.body: {next} costs more than this plan but allows fewer ads a day, so paying to move up the ladder buys less. Ad counts do not slide inside a band — they step at the boundary — which makes this the moment it is felt.

bandWarn.undercut: {plans} together cost GHS {price} and would give {ads} ads a day at {multiplier}× — more, for less money.
bandWarn.fix: Put the benefits on the line

finance.title: Finance

liability.label: Owed to users
liability.body: {points} points are held but not yet cashed out. This is not a cost yet, so it is not in the profit column — but profit read without it looks better than it is.

finance.exportNote: Exporting a statement as CSV for your accountant is backend work and is not wired up yet.

config.title: Platform settings
config.description: The numbers that decide how much money leaves. Every field maps to a live column — the name is printed under each one.

earning.title: Earning limits
earning.description: What one person can earn in a day, and how fast.

pool.title: Reward pool
pool.description: The platform-wide daily ceiling, across everybody.

payouts.title: Payout rules
payouts.description: When money is allowed to leave, and how long it waits first.

rate.title: Points and plans
rate.description: What a point is worth, and how plan benefits combine.

referrals.title: Referrals
referrals.description: What an invite is worth, and when it pays.

fraud.title: Fraud thresholds
fraud.description: The risk scores at which an account is rated medium, high or critical. These drive the risk labels on the payout queue.

killswitch.title: Kill switch
killswitch.description: One switch, for when something is badly wrong.

games.title: Games
games.description: The mystery box and the wheel. Prize tables live under Games; these are the switches around them.

leaderboard.title: Leaderboard and gift codes
leaderboard.description: What the public board counts and shows, and how hard a gift code is to guess at.

dailyCap.label: Daily points cap per user
dailyCap.description: The most any one account can earn in a UTC day, before plan multipliers.

cooldown.label: Cooldown between ads
cooldown.description: How long somebody waits after finishing one ad before the next can start.

retryCap.label: Attempts per ad
retryCap.description: How many times somebody may re-attempt an ad they got wrong.

poolCeiling.label: Daily ceiling for the whole platform
poolCeiling.description: Total points that may be minted across all users in a day.

poolBlocks.label: Stop earning at the ceiling
poolBlocks.description: On, reaching the ceiling halts earning for everyone until midnight UTC. Off, it only raises an alert and earning continues.
poolBlocks.warning: With this on, a busy day stops every user earning at once. Most operators leave it off and watch the alert instead.

payoutsEnabled.label: Payouts open
payoutsEnabled.description: The master switch. Off, users can still request but nothing can be approved or sent.

holdingHours.label: Holding window
holdingHours.description: How long a request waits before it can be approved. Time for the fraud checks to catch up.

cooloffHours.label: Cool-off after changing payout details
cooloffHours.description: How long after somebody changes their MoMo number or wallet before they can withdraw to it.

pointsRate.label: Points per cedi
pointsRate.warning: Forward-only. Changing this does not revalue points already earned — history keeps the rate it was written at. Raising it makes every future point worth less.

combineMode.label: How plan benefits combine
combineMode.description: When somebody holds more than one plan.

multiplierCeiling.label: Hard ceiling on the combined rate
multiplierCeiling.description: No stack of plans may exceed this, whatever the combine mode works out to.

referralSignup.label: Bonus on signup
referralSignup.description: Paid to the referrer the moment somebody signs up with their code.

referralSignupL2.label: Signup bonus, second level
referralSignupL2.description: Paid to whoever invited the referrer, for the same signup. Zero switches the second level of this stage off.

referralActivation.label: Bonus on activation
referralActivation.description: Paid once the referred person has actually watched some ads — the anti-farming half.

referralActivationL2.label: Activation bonus, second level
referralActivationL2.description: Paid to whoever invited the referrer, once the referred person has watched enough ads. Zero switches it off.

referralAds.label: Ads that count as activation
referralAds.description: How many completed ads before the activation bonus pays.

fraudMedium.label: Medium risk at
fraudMedium.description: Score at or above which a payout is labelled worth a look.

fraudHigh.label: High risk at
fraudHigh.description: Score at or above which a payout is labelled high risk.

fraudCritical.label: Critical risk at
fraudCritical.description: Score at or above which a payout says do not pay without checking.

earningPaused.label: Pause all earning, platform-wide
earningPaused.description: Nobody earns anything from any ad until this is switched back off.
earningPaused.warning: This stops every user on the platform immediately. Ads keep playing but award nothing, which users notice within minutes.

referralCommission.label: Commission when a referred person buys a plan
referralCommission.description: A percentage of what they pay, credited to whoever invited them as points. Flat — the inviter’s own plan does not change it. Zero switches this off completely.

referralCommissionL2.label: Commission, second level
referralCommissionL2.description: A percentage of the same purchase, credited to whoever invited the inviter. Paid out of what is left of the sale, so the two levels together can never exceed what was paid. Zero switches the second level off.

referralCommissionScope.label: Which purchases pay a commission
referralCommissionScope.description: Renewals are excluded by default. Because plans stack one of each, "each new plan" is capped at four commissions per invited person for all time.
referralCommissionScope.newPlans: Each new plan they buy, but not renewals

referralCommissionCap.label: Lifetime commission cap per invited person
referralCommissionCap.description: The most one invited person can ever earn their inviter from purchases. A purchase that crosses it pays the remainder. Zero means no limit.

gamesEnabled.label: Games are playable
gamesEnabled.description: Turns the mystery box and the wheel on for everyone. While off both screens are unreachable and no play can be made.
gamesEnabled.warning: Paying for more chances at a random prize is what a lottery is, and Ghana licenses games of chance separately from your money transfer licence. Have that cleared before turning this on.

gameCombineMode.label: Plays for stacked plans
gameCombineMode.description: How weekly plays combine when somebody holds several plans.
gameCombineMode.sumBonus: Add the bonuses, like ad caps (all four gives 11)

gameGap.label: Minimum gap between plays
gameGap.description: Stops a double tap or a stuck button spending two plays on one intention. Not a fraud control — the weekly allowance is that.

leaderboardRanks.label: Places shown on the leaderboard
leaderboardRanks.description: How far the public board goes. Somebody outside it still sees their own standing on a pinned row.

leaderboardGranted.label: Count gift codes, adjustments and game wins
leaderboardGranted.description: On, the board counts every credit a user receives. Off, it counts only what they earned from ads, surveys and referrals. Withdrawals never move the board either way.

leaderboardZeros.label: Show people who have earned nothing
leaderboardZeros.description: Off, the board lists only people with points. On, every active account appears, with the zeros last.

giftAttempts.label: Gift code guesses per hour
giftAttempts.description: How many wrong codes one account may try before being refused. The code space makes guessing hopeless; this makes trying pointless.

redemptionMinimum.label: Smallest withdrawal
redemptionMinimum.description: The fewest points anyone can withdraw — the same for everybody, whatever plans they hold. No plan has its own threshold.

redemptionFee.label: Withdrawal fee
redemptionFee.description: Percentage taken off each withdrawal to cover transaction costs and taxes. Frozen onto each request the moment it is filed.
redemptionFee.warning: Applies only to requests filed afterwards — anything already waiting keeps the rate it was quoted.

freeEarningDays.label: Free earning window
freeEarningDays.description: How many days after signing up a free account can earn. Buying any plan lifts it immediately. 0 means no limit. This is the ceiling on what a farmed account can ever be worth.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Who changed what, when, and what it was before. Newest first.

settings.title: Admin settings
settings.note: Administration of the administrators, rather than of the platform. Nothing here exists yet beyond the roles table.

settingsForm.unsaved: {count, plural, one {# unsaved change} other {# unsaved changes}}
settingsForm.savedCount: {count, plural, one {# setting updated.} other {# settings updated.}}

adminSettings.title: Admin settings

administrators.title: Administrators
administrators.description: Everyone who can get into this area, and what each of them may do.
administrators.note: Roles take effect immediately, in both directions: revoking somebody ends their access on their very next click, not when their session expires. Everything a role can do is written down in the migration that created it — support reaches the message queue, an ads manager reaches ads and advertisers, and everything else, including every payout, stays with a super admin.
administrators.noneProtected: No administrator has an authenticator yet. Turning on the requirement above will send them to enrol, not lock them out.
administrators.sent: Invitation sent to {email}. They set their own password from the link, and can turn on two-factor afterwards.
administrators.granted: That address already has an account, so no invitation was needed — the role applies the next time they sign in.
administrators.cannotRevokeSelf: You cannot revoke your own access
administrators.inviteHint: They get an email with a link that signs them in once and asks them to set a password. Until they do, they show as invited and cannot get in. Two-factor is theirs to turn on afterwards.
